test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: As announced by the Government of India, as on 7 July 2025, how many biotech startups does India have, compared to just 50 a decade ago?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nearly 11,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of **7 July 2025**, India has nearly **11,000 biotech startups**, according to the Government of India. This marks a significant growth from just **50 biotech startups a decade ago (2015)**.
 
• The biotech industry in India has been growing at a rapid pace due to increased **government initiatives, funding, and policy support** aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship in the sector.
 
• India's biotech sector is supported by initiatives like **Make in India** and **Startup India**, which encourage innovation in fields such as **healthcare, agriculture, bioinformatics, and industrial biotechnology**.
 
• The country is now among the top 12 biotech destinations globally and ranks **third in the Asia-Pacific region**.
 
• The establishment of biotech parks, incubators, and research institutions, coupled with government schemes, has created a **favorable ecosystem for startups** in the biotechnology domain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biotechnology Industry in India:**

 
 
• The Indian biotechnology industry is valued at approximately **$100 billion**, with projections to grow exponentially in the coming years.
 
• It is divided into five major segments: **biopharma, bioagriculture, bioindustry, bioinformatics, and bioservices**.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of vaccines in the world and is a major exporter of generic medicines and biopharmaceuticals.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Biotech Growth:**
 
 
• **Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC)**: A public sector enterprise that promotes innovation and entrepreneurship in the biotech industry by providing financial and infrastructural support.
 
• **National Biotechnology Development Strategy**: Aims to establish India as a global hub for biotechnology innovation and manufacturing by promoting research and entrepreneurship.
 
• **Startup India Initiative**: Provides funding, mentoring, and incubation support to startups, including those in biotechnology.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Biotechnology:**
 
 
• Used in healthcare for **drug development, gene therapy, and diagnostics**.
 
• Plays a vital role in agriculture through **genetically modified crops** and **biofertilizers**.
 
• Contributes to industrial applications such as **bioplastics, biofuels**, and **environmental conservation**.
 
 
 
• **Global Standing of Indian Biotechnology:**
 
 
• India ranks among the **top 12 biotech destinations globally** and is recognized for its **affordable innovation**.
 
• Major Indian biotech companies include **Biocon, Serum Institute of India, Panacea Biotech**, and **Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biotech Parks in India:**

 
 
• India has established numerous biotech parks, including **Genome Valley in Hyderabad**, the **Biotech Park in Lucknow**, and the **Biotechnology City in Bangalore**, to promote research, development, and entrepreneurship.
 
• These parks provide **state-of-the-art infrastructure, R&D facilities, and funding** opportunities for startups and researchers.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges in Biotech Sector:**
 
 
• Lack of sufficient funding for early-stage startups and **high R&D costs**.
 
• Stringent regulatory policies and **intellectual property issues** pose significant hurdles.
 
• Limited availability of skilled manpower in niche areas of biotechnology.
